pedagogicalReferences.title: Distraction Noise (The Cost of Switching)
pedagogicalReferences.whyItIsStrong: Communicates the abstract cognitive penalty of context switching using a single, intuitive horizontal conduit that sags under discrete physical weights, slowing flow speed live on screen.
pedagogicalReferences.primaryVisualIdea: Each interruption physically drops onto an attention beam, causing cumulative deflection and slowing the traveling focus pulse until single-tasking resets it to zero.
pedagogicalReferences.visualMechanism: Live SVG quadratic bezier deflection curve driven by spring-staged load drops, with a travelling flow pulse whose velocity is inversely coupled to deflection.
pedagogicalReferences.compositionStrategy: Centered minimalism with generous vertical breathing room. The conduit spans the horizontal axis (y=920); a single minimal percentage readout sits above it; zero clutter.
pedagogicalReferences.cameraStrategy: Static locked camera with subtle entrance scale. Lets the physical motion and deflection command 100% of viewer attention without camera motion noise.
pedagogicalReferences.temporalStrategy: Stepwise escalation: each spoken word beat drops a new node, culminating in severe strain at 14s, followed by an immediate, decisive elastic rebound and color shift to emerald at 17s.
pedagogicalReferences.whyItRemainsClear: Strict 3-tier hierarchy: exactly one primary mechanism (conduit), at most one supporting cue (capacity %), and pristine luminous ground with zero competing elements.
pedagogicalReferences.whatShouldBeLearned: How to represent an abstract mental tax as a live physical load; how to couple flow velocity to mechanical strain; how to make the resolution snap feel earned.
pedagogicalReferences.whatShouldNotBeCopied: Do not hardcode identical coordinates for unrelated clips; adapt the physical mechanism to what the new script actually means.

pedagogicalReferences.title: Structural Pressure (Why Small Pressures Break Us)
pedagogicalReferences.whyItIsStrong: Visually proves that duration, not mass, causes burnout: a single modest 1.0 KG weight never changes size, yet the monolithic architectural slab beneath it sags and fractures as time advances.
pedagogicalReferences.primaryVisualIdea: A constant weight held over progressive durations (1 min -> 1 hr -> 24 hrs -> 72 hrs) forces an architectural stone beam to sag 80px and propagate hairline stress fractures until released.
pedagogicalReferences.visualMechanism: Closed SVG polygon slab supported on dual pillars and anchored by a foundation datum line, mutating live with downward curvature and branching fracture strokes.
pedagogicalReferences.compositionStrategy: Architectural grounding. Dual vertical pillars frame the lateral space; the beam spans horizontally; the single weight sits dead center; negative space isolates the system.
pedagogicalReferences.cameraStrategy: Stationary, objective viewpoint. Gives the monolithic beam monumental physical stability, making its eventual bending and micro-cracking feel alarming.
pedagogicalReferences.temporalStrategy: Progressive accumulation across discrete time markers synchronized to voiceover timestamps, micro-tremor under chronic load, and an effortless upward spring release on resolution.
pedagogicalReferences.whyItRemainsClear: Zero unmotivated cards in the mechanism scenes. The viewer's eyes are drawn directly to the center where weight meets stone. Caption rests comfortably below in the bottom safe zone.
pedagogicalReferences.whatShouldBeLearned: Using an unchanging subject (1.0 KG weight) against a changing substrate (deforming beam) to make a conceptual argument without explanatory paragraphs.
pedagogicalReferences.whatShouldNotBeCopied: Avoid lifting weights without a narrative reason; the lift must correspond to an explicit spoken action of letting down the load.

agentContract.instructions: READ RIGHTMOTION_CREATIVE_CONSTITUTION.md AND THIS BRIEF BEFORE IMPLEMENTING Canvas.tsx. The Shot Director defines WHAT the viewer must see; the Retention Choreographer defines HOW attention behaves over time; you as the AI editor decide HOW to realize it. SIMPLE FRAME. RICH TIMELINE — Keep the screen simple. Keep the timeline alive.
agentContract.confidenceHierarchy:
CONSTITUTION > BRIEF > SHOT DIRECTIVES & ATTENTION PLAN > COMPONENT INDEX > AGENT IMPLEMENTATION.
REQUIRED: Narrative purpose, visual objective, primary visual idea, 5-question state change, and attention plan.
RECOMMENDED: Primary visual mechanism, composition mode, camera movement, and micro-events.
OPTIONAL: Suggested components (mutually optional options, NOT ingredients. Budget: 1).
agentContract.retentionPhilosophy: SIMPLE FRAME, RICH TIMELINE: A frame should be easy to understand at a glance. A sequence should remain dynamically interesting over time. visualDensity != attentionIntensity. Do not increase visual complexity merely to increase stimulation. Create retention through anticipation, timing, transformation, camera choreography, micro-events, contrast, and payoffs.
agentContract.simultaneousMotionBudget: Strict limit on simultaneous significant motion: exactly 1 primary moving system, and 0-1 subtle secondary cues. Never let presenter, physical mechanism, camera drift, animated cards, text slams, and particles move simultaneously.
agentContract.visualHierarchy: PRIMARY (one dominant visual idea) -> SECONDARY (at most one supporting detail) -> AMBIENT (context only; zero competition). Never multiple competing targets at once.
agentContract.noUnmotivatedCardification: Cards are permitted ONLY when they genuinely improve clarity or serve a justified narrative purpose (e.g. hero illustration card, product page worksheet proof, physical smartphone screen). A card must NEVER be used as a lazy default wrapper around text or icons.
agentContract.componentRestraint: suggestedComponents are MUTUALLY OPTIONAL candidates, NOT ingredients. Component budget defaults to 1 (max 2 for complex mechanisms). Prefer the smallest number of visual systems.
agentContract.temporalComplexity: Visual complexity exists in TIME rather than SPACE. Prefer one object with many meaningful states (stable -> pressure -> deflection -> fracture) over many objects with one simple state.
agentContract.fiveQuestionsRule: For every shot, you must satisfy: 1) What exists at the beginning? 2) What happens? 3) What visibly changes? 4) What exists at the end? 5) Why does that change matter? If only text changes, redesign the scene around physical or spatial transformation.
agentContract.minimalityPass: Before finalizing every major shot, execute the 'Remove One Thing' pass: What can be removed without losing meaning? Strip decorative particles, redundant metrics, and extra badges. If the physical motion already explains the idea, stop adding things.
